requirements.text: Collect the text, author and tags of every quote from all three versions (/, /js/, /scroll), keeping which version each quote came from.
Follow each version's pagination to its end: the Next links of / and /js/, and scrolling until the JSON API reports no next page; a version that stops early must not pass silently.
Record each quote once per version: no duplicates from scroll loads, retries, escalations or refetches, and no quote lost by the de-duplication mechanism.

One crawler, with one handler shared by the HTTP and browser fetches of the paginated versions; fetch over plain HTTP wherever the content is in the HTML (the plain version) and use a browser only for pages that need one.
In every browser fetch, images and fonts are not downloaded (blocked before the navigation).
On the scrolling version, take the quotes from the /api/quotes JSON responses the page loads, not from the DOM.
A page fetched over HTTP whose quotes are missing does not count as a success (it escalates to the browser or fails).

programs.notes: Two auto-tier Labels share one handler whose waitForCount escalates an empty HTTP page; an unscoped beforeNavigation route blocks images and fonts; the scroll handler reloads with waitForRequestFinished armed and reads each JSON page once, deduped by page number, and Records are deduplicated again after reading.

Forces http for the plain Label and browser for the JS and scroll Labels, with one shared handler; a forced-http page without quotes raises BrowserRequiredError, so it is not a success. A before-navigation response listener captures every /api/quotes page by number from the first load on, and the handler scrolls until has_next is false. Images and fonts are blocked before navigation.

Puts the plain and the JS versions on a single auto-tier Label. The stubs learn the tier per Label on a domain, so the escalating /js/ pages can teach that Label the browser tier, and the plain pages would then be fetched in a browser. The golden program uses two Labels for this reason. Everything else is sound: the route stream is driven beside serve, the reload has the waiter armed, and each page is awaited once by number.

One spider and one parse_listing callback: plain pages over HTTP and /js/ pages in Playwright with a wait_for_selector page method. An HTTP page without quotes is logged and counted as a failure. PLAYWRIGHT_ABORT_REQUEST blocks images and fonts. A response event handler collects each JSON page once, and a callable PageMethod scrolls until has_next is false or raises on a timeout.

api_misuses.member: AdaptivePlaywrightCrawler requestHandler context `page` (destructured in the handler's parameters)
api_misuses.assumed: Reading `page` is harmless on the HTTP-only run (the comment says it throws only for the scroll version).
api_misuses.doc_says: In the HTTP-only run, the context's `page` getter throws 'Page object was used in HTTP-only request handler' (crawlee 3.18.2 adaptive-playwright-crawler.js). Destructuring it fails every HTTP attempt, so every page, the plain ones included, is fetched in the browser, and detection stores clientOnly.

programs.notes: The resultChecker, the guarded pre-navigation route and the JSON capture by page number are right. However, the handler's `page` destructuring sends every request to the browser, so nothing is fetched over HTTP.

api_misuses.member: ctx.push (staged Records) with a program-side `recorded` Set
api_misuses.assumed: A quote is recorded once it has been pushed, so the handler skips its identity on any later run.
api_misuses.doc_says: push stages a Record with its attempt, and it is discarded if the attempt ends early. Sample-comparison runs and retries run the handler again, so a quote marked in the Set during a discarded run is never pushed in the run that commits.
The plain Label is fetch.tier auto, learned by sample comparison, so its pages can also be navigated in the browser, and a Hook scoped to the other Labels does not run there.

programs.notes: Has the auto-tier Labels, escalation on the wait, and a reload with the response waiter armed, with each JSON page read once. However, it de-duplicates in the handler with shared state, which can drop quotes, and the image and font blocking misses the plain Label's browser runs.

api_misuses.assumed: Blocks images and fonts of the browser fetch.
api_misuses.doc_says: The handler runs after the engine's navigation, so the first load's images and fonts are already downloaded. Only a before_navigation Hook installs a route before the browser navigates.

programs.notes: One handler for the three Labels with forced tiers, a reload with the expect_response armed, and a scroll loop over the JSON responses, with Records deduplicated after reading. Its route is registered only after the navigation, and the /js/ pages are reloaded to work around it, so every first browser load downloads images and fonts.

api_misuses.member: page.route stream answered inside the handler (with_resource_blocking)
api_misuses.assumed: Images and fonts are not downloaded in the browser.
api_misuses.doc_says: The handler runs after the navigation, so the escalated /js/ pages and the scroll page's first load have already downloaded their images and fonts; blocking before the navigation needs a before_navigation Hook.

programs.notes: Has the auto-tier Labels, a wait that escalates, per-version Datasets deduplicated on read, and a reload with the waiter armed for the JSON pages. Resource blocking starts only once the handler runs, after the browser has navigated.

One spider: HTTP first, a browser refetch for a page without quotes, and PLAYWRIGHT_ABORT_REQUEST blocking images and fonts. However, scroll_until_exhausted just returns when no new JSON response arrives within about 10 s, and an unparseable JSON page is only logged. A scroll that stops early therefore yields a partial version that is never marked failed.

api_misuses.member: AdaptivePlaywrightCrawler context enqueueLinks({ selector: 'li.next > a' }) in the browser
api_misuses.assumed: Enqueues nothing on a last page that has no Next link.
api_misuses.doc_says: In browser mode, enqueueLinks waits 5 s for its selector and throws when the selector is absent (crawlee 3.18.2 adaptive-playwright-crawler.js). The last /js/ page's handler therefore fails every retry, its pushes are not committed, and the request ends failed.

programs.notes: Has a custom always-static predictor with a resultChecker that escalates empty HTTP pages, a guarded pre-navigation route, and a JSON capture for the scroll page. However, the unconditional enqueueLinks in the browser loses the last /js/ page's quotes.
